title: Top 275 PDF: Words 51 to 75
subtitle: Splenetic to Stultify (SSC CGL 2026 Digital Notes)

words.meaning: Bad-tempered; spiteful and easily annoyed.
words.example: The irritable man snapped at everyone in the room.

words.meaning: Tending or able to change frequently or easily; versatile.
words.example: He is a protean actor capable of playing any role.

words.meaning: Larger or more generous than is usual or necessary.
words.example: The alumnus made a munificent donation to his college.

words.meaning: Dispute the truth, validity, or honesty of a statement or motive.
words.example: No one could impugn his integrity as an officer.

words.meaning: Deny or contradict a fact or statement.
words.example: No one can gainsay the importance of daily revision.

words.meaning: Speak badly of or tell lies about someone so as to damage their reputation.
words.example: They tried to defame him with false rumours.

words.meaning: Rebuke or scold severely.
words.example: The coach had to objurgate the players for their carelessness.

words.meaning: Root out and destroy completely.
words.example: Vaccination helped extirpate the deadly disease.

words.meaning: Censure or criticize severely.
words.example: The audit report excoriated the department for waste.

words.meaning: Report or represent in outline; foreshadow.
words.example: The minister's speech adumbrated the new economic policy.

words.meaning: Solemnly renounce a belief, cause, or claim.
words.example: The prince decided to renounce the throne.

words.meaning: Express disapproval of something.
words.example: Good teachers always deprecate cheating in exams.

words.hindi: खुलकर निंदा करना / कड़ी आलोचना करना
words.meaning: Speak or write about something with great hostility.
words.example: The activist continued to inveigh against corruption.

words.meaning: Atone for guilt or sin; make amends.
words.example: He worked for charity to expiate his past mistakes.

words.meaning: Speak or act in an evasive way to hide the truth.
words.example: When asked directly, the suspect began to prevaricate.

words.hindi: छोटी बात पर बहस करना / नुक्ताचीनी करना
words.meaning: Make petty or unnecessary objections.
words.example: He began to quibble over one rupee at the restaurant.

words.meaning: Harass someone persistently for or to do something; beg earnestly.
words.example: He continued to importune the committee for another chance.

words.meaning: Persuade someone to do something by means of deception or flattery.
words.example: He tried to inveigle his friend into joining the scheme.

words.meaning: Reprimand someone severely.
words.example: The judge castigated the police for the delay in investigation.

words.meaning: Render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible; bewilder.
words.example: Complex jargon often serves to obfuscate simple facts.

words.meaning: Turn into bone or bony tissue; become rigid or hardened.
words.example: The wet cement began to harden in the sun.

words.meaning: Spoil or impair the quality or efficiency of something.
words.example: A single forged signature can vitiate the entire contract.

words.meaning: Cause someone to feel drained of energy or vitality.
words.example: The scorching afternoon heat tends to enervate runners.

words.meaning: Make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse.
words.example: Scratching the rash will only exacerbate the itching.

words.hindi: रोकना / विकास बाधित करना / निष्प्रभाव करना
words.meaning: Cause to lose enthusiasm and initiative; hamper or hinder.
words.example: Too many rigid rules can stultify creativity in students.
